bullets.title: S&P 500 trend breakdown; McCullough signals sell-tech-bounces regime
bullets.body: Hedgeye's McCullough flagged an S&P 500 trend breakdown with a lower high and close below support at 7,631 on Friday; QQQ is down ~8% from cycle peak with a 10-12% drawdown triggering crash-mode signals. He removed MSFT, RBLX, ROKU, and ABNB from longs, recommends selling tech rebounds, and is rotating into consumer staples and healthcare. High-yield spreads widened ~17bps Friday, reinforcing defensive posture.

bullets.title: HFs now net underweight AI theme for first time since early 2023
bullets.body: Hedge fund net exposure to the AI theme fell to 34% vs. 35.4% market-cap weight — the first net underweight since early 2023 — following violent post-earnings reactions: INTC -29% (worst day ever), RDDT -29%, NOW -34%, FTNT -24%. About 60% of Russell 3000 stocks are down 20%+ since June, and cumulative HF degrossing has already exceeded 6% of the book. MS PB reports gross leverage at the 10th percentile vs. last year.

bullets.title: GS: Narrowest market breadth in 25 years; rotate to defensive quality
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs notes market breadth at a 25+ year low: 70% of S&P 500 companies are up post-earnings, but only 50% of market cap; the index is down 3% while S&P ex-AI is up 5%. GS recommends avoiding momentum factor risk and favors 23 defensive healthcare/staples names with high FCF yield and 5%+ 2027 EPS growth. Falling energy prices and interest rates in 2027 are expected to accelerate real income growth for the bottom income quintile, with the low-income consumer discretionary basket already +7% since October.

bullets.title: October ISM Manufacturing surges to 55.5, well above consensus
bullets.body: October ISM Manufacturing Index rose to 55.5 from 54.5, beating consensus of 54.5 and MS's own forecast of 52.4. Production and new orders strengthened, inventories expanded strongly (the biggest contributor to the headline), and supplier delivery times lengthened only modestly. Prices paid decelerated but remained elevated — a stagflationary undercurrent worth watching.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex came in light; 2027 consensus requires big step-up
bullets.body: 22V Research notes hyperscaler capex (GOOG, MSFT, META) undershot in Q3, and 2027 consensus requires a significant step-up from current run rates. AI winners baskets are characterized as likely to remain violently range-bound for up to 12 months, not just into year-end. Levered ETFs are contributing ~$16bn of selling per 1% SPX move, and macro systematic strategies are forecast net sellers of $10-15bn over the next week.

bullets.title: AI debt issuance at $655B YTD; credit standards tightening for hyperscalers
bullets.body: AI-linked debt issuance has reached $655B through mid-October 2026, with projections approaching $1T in new debt for 2027. Wall Street is tightening lending standards for AI infrastructure: CDS costs for hyperscalers hit their highest levels since 2021. ORCL launched a $20B combined debt-equity package (breaking its own pledge to limit gross debt growth to $10B through FY30), and MSFT filed a $25B debt offering — its first IG bond sale in over 9 years.

bullets.title: Anti-Minsky thesis: persistent AI worry prevents bubble formation
bullets.body: A circulated note argues that AI's accelerating innovation pace creates a structural time mismatch between capital commitment duration and technology change velocity, preventing the synchronized crowding needed for a classic bubble. Rolling repricing across SaaS, credit, and memory replaces a single violent collapse, and wider credit spreads reflect the market's immune system functioning, not a bubble bursting. Embodied AI (robotics, autonomous vehicles) is flagged as the next wave of capital disruption.

bullets.title: OpenAI cuts Series C target to $20B from $30B; valuation reset to $1.25T
bullets.body: OpenAI has downsized its funding round from $30B to $20B and reset its valuation target from $1.4T to $1.25T. Separately, Anthropic plans to raise up to $3.5B in Japan as part of its IPO roadshow, which kicks off mid-November. The tighter OpenAI financing is seen as pressuring expansion economics for AI infrastructure counterparties.

bullets.title: Data center capacity +180GW by 2030 but new cost/financing constraints emerging
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley forecasts global data center capacity additions of +180GW at +23% pa through 2030 (US +88GW, China +49GW, Europe +12GW). Beyond power (the primary obstacle), new constraints are emerging: financing selectivity, building cost inflation trending >10% YoY, powered land availability, and chips/GPUs. The US faces a power shortfall through 2028, and AI-related debt issuance is at 2.2x last year's rate YTD but credit markets are becoming more selective.

bullets.title: DRAM prices +12% M/M, +15.5% Q/Q on AI datacenter demand; tight into 2H27
bullets.body: KeyBanc reports October 8Gb DDR5 DRAM pricing +12.0% m/m and +15.5% q/q, with DDR4 up 21.2% m/m and 35.7% q/q. AI datacenter demand is outpacing DRAM supply; Samsung and MU expect tight conditions into 2028, SK Hynix into 2030. HBM4 trades at >3x wafer ratio vs DDR5, further constraining conventional DRAM supply. NAND is broadly flat m/m but +0.3% q/q with datacenter expected to become the largest NAND market in 2026.

bullets.title: Foreign PMIs soften; PSC model sees global manufacturing cooling to 50.2% by Sep 2027
bullets.body: PSC's preliminary October Foreign Manufacturing PMI slipped 0.1ppt to 51.5%, with Korea down 2.6ppt to 51.3% and Taiwan down 1.9ppt to 54.9% — both still expansionary but fading. France is already contractionary at 49.5% with 10-year OAT yields above nominal GDP growth. PSC's model forecasts Foreign Mfg PMI cooling to 50.2% by September 2027, barely expansionary; MSCI EAFE is off 5% from its September record high.

bullets.title: UBS: October nonfarm payrolls expected ~63k; soft hiring undermines staffing rallies
bullets.body: UBS forecasts October nonfarm payrolls around 63k — above September's ~29k but still within a low-hire environment — with unemployment likely holding at 4.2%. Temporary help staffing is down ~18% since March 2022 while overall payrolls grew 6%; penetration rates at 1.56% are unlikely to inflect near term. UBS maintains Sell ratings on RHI and EFOR despite 65-84% rallies over six months.

bullets.title: META planning massive multi-tranche bond offering; NVDA/AMD/AVGO eyeing $5B equity stake
bullets.body: Meta has tasked Citi and Morgan Stanley with investor calls for a potential five-part USD and six-part EUR bond offering, supported by its Aa3/AA- ratings. NVIDIA, AMD, and Broadcom have indicated interest in purchasing up to an aggregate $5B of Meta Class A common stock. Meta targets $135-145B capex in 2026, funded via operating cash flow, investment-grade debt, strategic partnerships, and equity. S&P separately downgraded META's outlook from stable to negative, citing high capex and negative FCF.

bullets.title: MRVL acquires LITE in $115B all-stock deal — one of the largest tech transactions ever
bullets.body: Marvell Technology announced an all-stock acquisition of Lumentum at 4.5 MRVL shares per LITE share, implying a ~$115B enterprise value and closing targeted for 1H 2028. MRVL shareholders retain ~2/3 of the combined entity; management targets >$1B in annual synergies with EPS accretion starting 2029 and a combined TAM of $550B. LITE is down ~4% and MRVL down ~2% in pre-market; UBS rates MRVL Buy at $350 PT and LITE Neutral at $960 PT.

bullets.title: GOOGL search revenue headwind deepens as AI Overviews penetration hits 82%
bullets.body: Wells Fargo cut FY27/FY28 Google search revenue estimates by 2 points each (now +7.7%/+9.6%) as AI Overviews penetration reached 82% globally, up ~7pts in October. Paid clicks/session correlation to US desktop AI Overviews penetration is -0.97 from 2Q24 to 3Q26, with paid clicks growth expected at +4% in 4Q26 and 0% in 1Q27 before recovering in 2Q27. Google is pushing AI Overviews aggressively despite the business model not yet offsetting suppressed clicks with higher CPCs or new ad units.

bullets.title: MSFT Azure accelerates to 48% YoY; guided to 49-50% in 2QFY27
bullets.body: Truist flags Microsoft Azure growth accelerated to 48% y/y in 1QFY27 (up from 43% in 4QFY26) and guided to 49-50% in 2QFY27. GitHub Copilot Fusion now scores within two points of Claude Code Opus 5.5 Max at ~50% API cost and 40% faster execution. Anthropic's Claude for Government users grew 8x since February with federal agency usage up 20x y/y.

bullets.title: FOXA F1Q27 blowout: revenue +22% YoY, EBITDA +54% YoY on World Cup and political ads
bullets.body: Fox Corp. reported F1Q27 revenue of $4.57B (+22% YoY, beating consensus $4.32B) and adj. EBITDA of $1.64B (+54% YoY, beating consensus $1.36B). TV advertising revenues rose 60% YoY driven by World Cup, political ads, and Tubi (+35% YoY); a record mid-term political ad cycle of $350M+ is expected. FOX One subscriber acquisition grew 30% YoY during football season with 97% of subs new to cable, characterized as incremental not cannibalistic. UBS upgraded to Buy.

bullets.title: ITC extension probability ~80% post-midterms; no extension implies 50%+ power price jump
bullets.body: Roth notes the solar ITC extension carries roughly 80% probability post-midterms. Without extension, mid-US solar power prices could jump from ~$65/MWh to ~$95/MWh (50%+). ITC extension timing is critical: Q2/Q3 2027 action salvages 2029-2031 projects; a late 2028/early 2029 extension leaves 2030-2031 projects in jeopardy.

bullets.title: DASH to acquire CART for ~$17B; shifts fulfillment leverage away from grocers
bullets.body: DoorDash announced an acquisition of Instacart at $65/share (~$17B equity value). Morgan Stanley notes this could shift negotiating leverage toward platforms and pressure grocery retailers (KR, ACI, SFM) reliant on outsourced fulfillment; WMT and TGT are viewed as relatively insulated via their proprietary Spark and Shipt networks. Separately, DASH has reportedly received 'several hundred' orders from AI agents.

bullets.title: McCullough buys UUP and BNO; energy and USD positioning shift
bullets.body: Hedgeye's Keith McCullough added 100bps UUP (dollar long) and 50bps BNO (crude oil) to his portfolio while reducing oil long to minimum exposure overall — suggesting tactical commodity/FX positioning around macro uncertainty. WTI trade support is cited at $97, trend support at $91; Dec WTI crude is down 6.4% to $97.47 in pre-market.
